verdict.printed: Handwritten library shelfmark 'V / B130.7 / M67 / 1' on the dark purple cover of a thread-bound volume; nothing else is printed
verdict.evidence: The English has '->B130.7<- ->M67<- ->1<-', which matches the handwritten shelfmark on page 65. Page 66 has the same shelfmark but with '2' instead of '1'. The summary and keywords only describe this cover.

verdict.printed: Page 2 is a half-title that reads 'THEOSOPHIA PRACTICA' and has a library stamp and handwritten shelf marks (~875, 8° Z. 14610).
verdict.evidence: 'PRACTICAL THEOSOPHY' with the shelf marks '~ 875' and '8° Z. 14610' are all printed or written on page 2.

verdict.printed: Nothing: page 25 is a blank endpaper spread (the right leaf is pasted to the blue cover), with only faint show-through.
verdict.evidence: 'This leaf is blank and contains no printed text or illustration' correctly describes page 25 and adds no content from page 24 or page 26.

verdict.printed: Page 94 is a blank-ruled leaf. Its margin reads 欽定四庫全書 目錄一, and its last column has the table-of-contents title 皇朝禮器圖式目錄一 (Huangchao Liqi Tushi, Table of Contents 1).
verdict.evidence: The English 'The illustrations within Lu Dian's Images of Ritual were merely attempts to model after ancient artifacts... arranged and compiled the following' renders 圖陸佃禮象徒規撫舊物已也謹詮次如右, which is printed on page 93. Its 'Page 23' is page 93's leaf number (二十三). Page 94's own title, 目錄一, is never rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 243 is a divisional title page that reads only "THE APPENDIXES.", with text from the other side of the leaf showing through.
verdict.evidence: "# THE APPENDIXES." is printed on page 243. The summary line "This leaf carries the divisional title heading for the appendixes" isn't printed on any page; it's a short added description.

verdict.printed: Page 44 has the title 划船 (paddle boat, read right to left as 船划) and a woodcut of a man poling a small boat loaded with bundles of rice seedlings, with a willow on the bank and two peaks behind.
verdict.evidence: The title 'Carving the Boat' and the picture description render page 44, but the title is mistranslated: 划 was misread as 刻. It should be 'Paddle Boat' (划船), which page 45's text explains. The description also leaves out the bundles of seedlings in the boat.

verdict.printed: Page 60 has the title 淫羊藿 (Yinyanghuo) over a woodcut of the Epimedium plant. The left margin carries the book's running title and a folio number.
verdict.evidence: '# Yinyanghuo (Epimedium)' renders the title printed at the top of page 60, and the note describes the woodcut on page 60. Of the margin text, only one character ('Three') is rendered; the rest is marked unclear.

verdict.printed: Page 88 has the two-character title 鷫鷞 (sushuang, a legendary water bird) above a woodblock picture of a long-necked bird perched on a gnarled, leafless tree.
verdict.evidence: The heading '# Cormorant' renders page 88's title, and the note describes page 88's picture. However, the title is mistranslated: the transcription's 鸕鷀 is wrong, and the scan shows 鷫鷞, the bird described on page 89 ('鷫鷞水鳥蓋雁屬也'). So 'Cormorant' and the summary and keywords that call it a cormorant are wrong.

verdict.printed: Page 94 is the closing leaf of table of contents 1. It has the trailing title 皇朝禮器圖式目錄一 in the left column, the margin header 欽定四庫全書 and the label 目錄一, and empty columns everywhere else.
verdict.evidence: 'Illustrated Regulations for Ceremonial Paraphernalia of the Imperial Court: Table of Contents 1' renders 皇朝禮器圖式目錄一, which is printed on page 94. The header 'Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, Table of Contents 1' matches the margin text on page 94. The summary only describes this same leaf.

verdict.printed: Page 6: the heading 鼎 (Ding) above a woodcut of a four-legged rectangular bronze vessel with two upright handles, patterned sides and curved legs.
verdict.evidence: '# Ding' renders the heading 鼎 printed on page 6, and the note describes page 6's woodcut. The gloss 'ritual bronze vessel' is a short addition that isn't printed on any page. None of the English draws on page 5's list of vessel names or on page 7's essay 鼎鼐總說.

verdict.printed: A single handwritten note: '8 προσοίκων - neighbours' (a gloss on line 8 of p.167, where the word is underlined)
verdict.evidence: 'additions - <unclear>περιεχόντων</unclear>' is an attempt at page 168's handwritten note. It misreads προσοίκων as προσθήκων and leaves the English gloss 'neighbours' as unclear Greek.

verdict.printed: Running head '86 AROMATVM HIST.', an unlabelled woodcut of the nutmeg fruit, husk, mace-covered seed and two seeds, and the catchword 'De'
verdict.evidence: 'HISTORY OF AROMATICS' translates the running head 'AROMATVM HIST.' printed on page 92, and the note describes page 92's nutmeg woodcut. 'catchword: Of' renders the catchword 'De' on page 92. The summary and keywords only describe this page.

verdict.printed: Half-title page with only 'BOOK VI' printed on it
verdict.evidence: '# BOOK VI' is the only body text, and it matches the title printed on page 175; the summary just describes that title

verdict.printed: Page 81 is a woodcut illustration of a leafy flowering plant. Its margin caption reads 資州生瓜菜 and its section label reads 蔬類卷之四.
verdict.evidence: 'Zizhou raw melon greens' and 'Vegetables section, fascicle four' render the caption and the section label printed on page 81. Nothing from page 80 (胡瓜) or page 82 (the 宋圖經 text) appears.

verdict.printed: Page 457 is a digitization target sheet: a drawing of a damaged open book captioned 'Texte détérioré — reliure défectueuse' and 'NF Z 43-120-11'
verdict.evidence: 'Deteriorated text, defective binding' and 'NF Z 43-120-11' are printed on page 457. The summary adds a short gloss that the sheet 'conforms to standard' NF Z 43-120-11, which is minor.

verdict.printed: Page 32 has the title 預知子 (Yuzhizi) above a woodcut of a vine climbing a bamboo pole beside a rock.
verdict.evidence: 'Yuzhizi' renders the title printed on page 32, and the note describes page 32's picture. The gloss 'Akebia fruit' and keywords like 'medicinal plant' are small additions that aren't printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 60 is a full-page woodcut of Epimedium with the title 淫羊藿 at the top, plus partly cut-off marginal text at the left edge (the running head and a folio number, 二十).
verdict.evidence: 'Dahurian Angelica grows in the river valleys and low-lying marshes of the East-of-the-River region... The people of Chu call this plant Yao' renders the 白芷 entry printed on page 59. Only the title 'Epimedium' and the stray '... Three' come from page 60. The added gloss 'as a symbol of the noble heart' is printed on no page.

verdict.printed: Page 19 is a full-page woodcut of the fern 碎補 (Suibu) with its roots. The margin reads 植物名實圖考, 碎補 and 石草卷之十七.
verdict.evidence: 'Stone and Rock Herbs, Scroll Seventeen' renders the margin label 石草卷之十七 on page 19. However, 'Supplementary Inscriptions' mistranslates the plant name 碎補 (misread as 碑補), and the English does not describe the illustration.

verdict.printed: Page 57 is an illustration with two labels, 狼牙拍 (wolf-tooth clapper board) and 飛鈎 (flying hook). The margin reads 三才圖會 器用八卷 廿一.
verdict.evidence: 'Wolf-tooth club, flying hook, Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms ... volume eight ... Twenty-one' renders the labels and margin text printed on page 57. The descriptive text about these tools is on page 58 and is not rendered here. 器用 is loosely given as 'Appended utility'.

verdict.printed: Page 70: the title 倚樹圖 ('Illustration of Leaning Against a Tree') printed vertically beside a woodcut of a robed man resting one hand on a tree trunk and holding a round fan in the other; the edge of the neighbouring leaf's margin is just visible
verdict.evidence: 'Illustration of Leaning Against a Tree' renders the title 倚樹圖 printed on page 70; the note describes page 70's picture of a man leaning on a tree and holding a round object

verdict.printed: Page 70 has only the title 倚樹圖 ('Illustration of Leaning on a Tree') beside a woodcut of a man in robes resting his hand on a tree trunk and holding a round fan.
verdict.evidence: 'Illustration of Waving a Fan' (揮扇圖) and the feather-fan description render page 69. The paragraphs on Zhuge Liang and strategists are commentary printed on no page. The English never mentions 倚樹圖 (page 70).

verdict.printed: Page 69: the title 軒轅集 (Xuanyuan Ji), the margin header 三才圖會 人物十五卷 with a leaf number, and a woodcut of Xuanyuan Ji riding a tiger with a pole and basket over his shoulder, a snake below, and a gnarled tree on the right.
verdict.evidence: '# Xuanyuan Ji' renders the title printed on page 69, and the header renders page 69's margin header. The note describes page 69's picture of the man on a tiger with a snake. Nothing from page 70's biography (his centuries of age, the bottomless wine pot, Emperor Xuanzong) appears.

verdict.printed: Page 44 has the title 划船 ('paddle boat'), wrongly transcribed as 刻船, above a woodcut of a long narrow boat with a pole and bundles of seedlings on a river, with willows and rocky hills behind.
verdict.evidence: 'Mountain-Excursion Boat … two, four, six, or eight … incapable of breaking the waves' renders the 遊山船 text printed on page 43. The heading 'Engraved Illustrations of Boats' comes from the misread title 刻船, so page 44's real title 划船 is never rendered and the picture is not described.

verdict.printed: Running title 三才圖會 人事三卷 with folio number 二十八, and a two-column grid of eight model brush strokes (right column: ㇏, ㇏, ㇗, ㇄ shapes; left column: ㇇, 乙, ㇖, ㇕ shapes)
verdict.evidence: 'Collected Illustrations of the Three Realms, Human Affairs, Fascicle 3' and 'Twenty-eight' render page 74's printed header and folio. The stroke grid matches page 74's diagram. The added note and summary only describe this page's picture.

verdict.printed: Page 32 is a blank verso. Only the mirror-image show-through of plate 13 on page 31 is visible: the lab panels, Sol and Luna, a reversed '13', and the numbers '100·1000 10000 &c'.
verdict.evidence: '100-1000' / '10.000' and the panel description ('figures handle flasks… stand beside Sol and Luna near a large furnace') are plate 13's content, printed on page 31 and seen through the leaf. 'Massen' and '100-200' are misreadings of the reversed numbers and are printed on no page.

verdict.printed: Page 481: Russian prose comparing Julian with Constantine, assessing Julian's reign and death, and how Constantine's line ended, followed by a footnote
verdict.evidence: The English has only the single word "thoughtful" plus a summary saying the leaf bears just that word. That word is printed on none of the three pages, and page 487's full printed text is not rendered.

verdict.printed: Title page: DISCOVRS DE LA CAVSE DE LA PESANTEVR. Par C. H. D. Z., printer's device with a laurel wreath, A LEIDE, Chez PIERRE VANDER AA, Marchand Libraire. MDCXC.
verdict.evidence: 'DISCOURSE ON THE CAUSE OF GRAVITY. By C. H. D. Z.' and 'AT LEIDEN ... 1690' render the title page printed on page 137. The note describing the printer's device and the summary naming Huygens are only short metadata.

verdict.printed: Page 88 is the end-of-volume colophon line 太乙金鏡式經卷二 ('Taiyi Golden Mirror Divination Classic, Volume Two'), with the margin header 欽定四庫全書 / 卷二
verdict.evidence: 'Taiyi Golden Mirror Formulae Classic, Volume Two' renders 太乙金鏡式經卷二, which is printed on page 88. The 'Great Monad' gloss and the summary/keywords are small additions.

verdict.printed: Page 626: running header 'Artis Magnæ Consoni, & Dissoni' over nine systems of mensural music notation with '4' figures marking fourths, and no prose
verdict.evidence: 'The Great Art of Consonance and Dissonance' translates the running header on page 677, and the note describing nine staves with the numeral '4' matches that page's music

verdict.printed: Page 499 has only an engraving of a Rithmomachia board, with numbered round, triangular and square pieces (2, 4, 6, 9, 15, 25 / 4, 16, 20, 25, 45, 81 / 6, 36, 42, 49, 91, 169 / 8, 64, 72, 81, 153, 289), including a stacked pyramid marked 91.
verdict.evidence: '->6. 36. 42. 49. 91. 169.<-' matches the numbers on the pieces in the page 499 engraving, and the note is a short description of that picture. Page 498 shows the opposing pieces (49, 28, 16…) and page 500 is a faint ghost image; neither is rendered here.

verdict.printed: Title page heading: ΝΟΝΝΟΥ ΤΟΥ ΠΑΝΟΠΟΛΙΤΟΥ ΔΙΟΝΥΣΙΑΚΩΝ ΔΩΔΕΚΑΤΟΝ (Nonnus of Panopolis, Dionysiaca, Book Twelve), with bleed-through from the facing leaf
verdict.evidence: 'By Nonnus of Panopolis / Dionysiaca / Book Twelve' renders the centered title printed on page 265

verdict.printed: Page 55 has the margin title 墨苑玄工 and the chapter mark 卷一二. In the middle is a round seal-like inscription, 龍鳳呈祥 ("Dragon and Phoenix Bring Good Fortune"). The block-maker's mark 滋蘭堂 is at the bottom of the margin.
verdict.evidence: "Mysterious Craft of the Ink Garden" and "Volume 12" come from page 55's margin. "A Dragon Presented / An Auspicious Phoenix" renders page 55's central 龍鳳呈祥, though the reading order is wrong: it should be one phrase, "Dragon and Phoenix Bring Good Fortune". The summary only describes these same items.

verdict.printed: Page 124 has a one-line engraved title, 'S'il aduenoit un lieu triengullaire à fortifier, brief et le pire, mais ainsi l'egaller aura forteresse entiere', above an engraving of a triangular star fort with a moat and outworks.
verdict.evidence: 'If a triangular site were to be fortified, in short the worst, but evening it out in this manner will produce a complete fortress' renders the title printed on page 124. The note only describes page 124's engraving.

verdict.printed: Copyright notice 'ALLE RECHTE, EINSCHLIESSLICH DES ÜBERSETZUNGSRECHTS, VORBEHALTEN.', plus a handwritten call number (BL 775 / R43 / 1920) and a mirrored UNIV. OF CALIFORNIA stamp
verdict.evidence: 'ALL RIGHTS, INCLUDING THE RIGHT OF TRANSLATION, RESERVED.' renders the copyright notice printed on page 8. The call number transcribed as '1900.' looks like '1920' in the scan, but that is a handwritten marking, not printed text.

verdict.printed: Page 88 is the blank closing leaf of Scroll Two. It has only the end-title 太乙金鏡式經卷二 and the margin label 卷二.
verdict.evidence: The body lines 'In the first year of the Yongxing era of Emperor Hui of the Jin Dynasty... entered the Second Epoch' through 'twelfth year of the Kaiyuan era... Third Epoch' and the folio number 'Twelve' (十二) are all printed on page 87. Page 88's own end-title, 'Taiyi Golden Mirror Divination Classic, Scroll Two', is rendered.
